name: PC and Mobile Optimization
description: optimziing the entire codebase for both pc and mobile.

goal.answer: Make the Manarat Science Club codebase render correctly, performantly, and accessibly across phone (≥390px), tablet, and desktop — meeting Lighthouse mobile ≥ 90 / desktop ≥ 95 and zero axe-core WCAG 2.1 AA violations on every route, with touch targets ≥ 44x44 CSS px, no horizontal overflow at 390px, and no CLS regressions.

criteria.answer: C1: Lighthouse mobile Performance ≥ 90 and Accessibility = 100 on every public route (home, /blogs, /blogs/[slug], /events, /join, /legacy, /opportunities, /achievements, /profile, /signin, /signup). Method: npx lighthouse run against pnpm start after build, mobile form-factor. C2: Lighthouse desktop Performance ≥ 95 and Accessibility = 100 on every public route. Method: same as C1 with --preset=desktop. C3: Zero axe-core WCAG 2.1 AA violations on every public route. Method: axe DevTools panel sweep per route at 390px and 1280px, results recorded. C4: No horizontal overflow at 390px viewport on any route (documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390). Method: DevTools device toolbar manual check per route, recorded in perf-report.md. C5: All interactive elements (links, buttons, inputs) have touch target ≥ 44x44 CSS px on mobile viewports. Method: DevTools device toolbar inspection at 390px, recorded in perf-report.md. C6: Core Web Vitals on mobile (Slow 4G): LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms on every public route. Method: Lighthouse mobile report, recorded in perf-report.md. C7: All and next/image usages set explicit width/height or use fill with a sized parent. Zero layout-shift from missing dimensions. Method: grep audit + Lighthouse CLS confirmation. C8: pnpm build and pnpm lint exit 0 with zero errors and zero new warnings introduced by this work. C9: CMS dashboard routes (/cms, /cms/posts, /cms/posts/new, /cms/posts/[id]/edit, /cms/tags, /cms/users) are usable on 390px viewports (no overflow, controls reachable, tables become cards or scroll). Method: DevTools device toolbar sweep at 390px, recorded in perf-report.md. C10: A before/after Lighthouse report is committed as .kimchi/docs/perf-report.md showing baseline scores, final scores per route, and a per-route changelog of fixes.

constraints.answer: Verification via Lighthouse only — no Playwright visual tests, no axe automation; axe checks done via DevTools panel., Tiered sequencing: public marketing pages first (home, blogs, events, achievements), then public utility pages (join, legacy, opportunities, profile), then auth + CMS last., 390px minimum baseline (standard phone). 768px tablet and 1280px desktop are also verified but not separately mobile-targeted., WCAG 2.1 AA a11y target — contrast, focus, labels, keyboard nav., Do not change visual design, content, or branding; only behavior, structure, and technical implementation., Do not introduce heavy new UI dependencies. next/dynamic, next/image, next/font, prefers-reduced-motion, existing radix primitives are the toolbox., pnpm build and pnpm lint must remain clean throughout., Lottie, GSAP, motion, TipTap are required design elements — optimize via lazy loading and reduced-motion respect, do not remove.

phases.answer: Foundations & Baseline, Public Marketing Tier (High-Traffic), Public Utility Tier (Long Tail), Auth + CMS Tier, Cross-Cutting Sign-off

assumptions.answer: Lottie/GSAP/motion/TipTap are required design elements, not removable; optimization means lazy loading and prefers-reduced-motion respect, not removal. A Lighthouse mobile score ≥ 90 and desktop ≥ 95 is achievable without rewriting components from scratch. The current codebase has no Playwright setup, and Lighthouse-only verification means I will not add Playwright. Visual design (colors, layout structure, content) is preserved — only code-level performance, responsive correctness, interaction UX, and a11y are in scope. "Tiered priority" follows existing route visibility: marketing pages (home, blogs, events, achievements) first; utility pages (join, legacy, opportunities, profile) second; auth + CMS third. The three heavy Lottie files on the homepage are loaded from the lottie.host CDN — I will convert these to next/dynamic imports but keep the same URLs. Raw img tags (e.g. /memberimage/*.png on the homepage editorial) will be converted to next/image with explicit dimensions; existing paths and alt text are preserved. The sentry-example-page route is a Next.js default debug page, not part of the user's product, and will be skipped. CMS Lighthouse thresholds are slightly relaxed (mobile ≥ 85, desktop ≥ 90) because the CMS is admin-only and includes the TipTap editor which inherently carries weight; axe WCAG AA remains strict.

Audit font loading via next/font, viewport meta, theme-color; nav mobile menu focus trap and keyboard nav; footer grid and link touch targets. Reusable utilities (cn, a11y hooks) introduced here so later phases can apply them. Baseline scores recorded for every route.
